targeting_gate.verbatim_anchor:
The species’-range impact model is derived from the focal point seed zone method of
Parker (1992; Parker and van Niejenhuis 1996), a site-specific approach to defining seed
procurement zones for regeneration. This method may be used for genetically variable,
wide-ranging tree species adapted to local environmental conditions, a pattern common
among many North American tree species. Using the focal point seed zone method, an
individual site to be regenerated becomes the focal point, and a unique seed procurement
zone is established for that site as needed. This method requires two sources of data: (1)
provenance trial data derived from multiple common garden growth trials of multiple seed
sources collected from populations located at various geographic points within a region;
and (2) climatic data for those geographic points of population origin.
targeting_gate.rationale: Given planting site is focal point; method selects seed provenances for white spruce under climates. Species-only procurement model does not select practice implementation area.

key_findings: Screen only; species-specific seedsource portfolio, not afforestation siting.
holds: No generic climate threshold or species-unit extraction under user gate.
completion_boundary: Source-purpose screening and documented passages only; no claim of complete main-paper/supplement extraction, source sweep, human approval or executable mapping.
